issues.competing_evidence: Joshi+20 infer 49±2 MG from the n=5/6 cyclotron humps for T=10 keV and θ=90 deg. Beuermann+21 fit cyclotron humps with 36 MG at T=10 keV, θ=70 deg, logΛ=2 and do not confirm the Joshi emission lines; a possible Hα σ− trough could imply 34 MG in an accretion halo. Harrison & Campbell+15 give separate WISE branches B≥35 or ≤20 MG and a color-based B≤30 MG suggestion. Barrett+20 has 3563±730 G conditional radio-emission-region ECM field.
issues.why_it_matters: These diagnostics measure different regions and model assumptions; selecting one number would distort WD-field comparisons across magnetic CVs and other radio populations.
issues.needed_action: Decide whether to show the distinct model-based cyclotron/halo constraints separately in population summaries or select a diagnostic-specific value; do not average them or equate the kG radio-plasma value to a WD field.

issues.competing_evidence: Joshi+20 calls RX J0859 an eclipsing polar and interprets ≈1.1 mag R-band dips as eclipses. Beuermann+21 analyzes optical minima over 1996–2019, calls the system noneclipsing, and attributes minima to cyclotron beaming; a wide X-ray dip may be stream absorption. Beuermann’s ephemeris uses 24 minima and identifies a cycle-count issue in the Joshi 2014 timings.
issues.why_it_matters: Geometry informs inclination constraints, mass models and comparisons of eclipsing versus noneclipsing polars.
